# Functional analysis and harmonic analysis

The pinned Mathlib supplies Fourier analysis on the circle and the logarithmic Mellin change of variable. TauCeti supplies a distributional Schwartz kernel theorem in Euclidean charts. GaussianField supplies the Hermite basis and nuclearity of real Euclidean Schwartz spaces. These are useful at different points of the argument.

| Sections and pages | Verified precedent and scope | Remaining mathematical work |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1, pp. 155–161. Schauder bases and Dynin–Mityagin | Mathlib `GeneralSchauderBasis` is defined on a normed space. GaussianField gives `GaussianField.DyninMityaginSpace.hasSum_basis` and `GaussianField.DyninMityaginSpace.toNuclearSpace` from coefficient data on a real locally convex space. [Dynin–Mityagin expansion](https://github.com/mrdouglasny/gaussian-field/blob/1283a2721377a36e80672799fcc1f69a494c8ea0/Nuclear/NuclearSpace.lean) | Masullo 4.1.2.6 deduces absoluteness for **every** equicontinuous Schauder basis in a nuclear complex space. The library proves the expansion for a supplied basis and proves nuclearity in the other direction. Masullo cites Jarchow, §21.10, Thm. 1, p. 510. |
| 4.2, 4.4–4.6, pp. 161–174 and 188–220. Periodic expansions | `GaussianField.periodizeCLM` continuously periodizes real Schwartz functions onto a smooth circle. `GaussianField.SmoothMap_Circle.hasSum_fourierBasis` gives a smooth-topology expansion. For complex functions, `TauCeti.UnitAddTorus.tendstoUniformly_iteratedFDeriv_sum_mFourier` gives uniform convergence through derivative order k for K derivatives with K > dimension + k. [periodization](https://github.com/mrdouglasny/gaussian-field/blob/1283a2721377a36e80672799fcc1f69a494c8ea0/SchwartzNuclear/Periodization.lean) · [circle expansion](https://github.com/mrdouglasny/gaussian-field/blob/1283a2721377a36e80672799fcc1f69a494c8ea0/SmoothCircle/Nuclear.lean) · [complex torus](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/8794ab329bb60340fa690a2902cf995f0571721b/TauCeti/Analysis/Fourier/Torus/Decay.lean) | Transport by log to the quotient of the positive reals by a cyclic subgroup and rescale its period. Impose the paper’s support, exponential weights, isotypes and multiplicity conditions separately. |
| 4.3, pp. 174–188. Isotypic projectors | `TauCeti.hasSum_peterWeyl_expansion` gives an L² expansion on compact groups with normalized Haar measure and a complete set of models for the irreducibles. Mathlib `fourierBasis` handles the circle. [Peter–Weyl](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/8794ab329bb60340fa690a2902cf995f0571721b/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Compact/PeterWeyl.lean) · [circle basis](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/AddCircle.lean) | Apply to the compact norm-one factor. Prove continuity of the averaging projectors in the locally convex topology used on the full space. |
| 7.1–7.2, pp. 312–340. Polar multiplicities and principal parts | Mathlib `meromorphicOrderAt` and `MeromorphicNFAt.meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg_iff_analyticAt` handle pole orders, including vector-valued functions with normed target. [order](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/Meromorphic/Order.lean) · [normal form](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/Meromorphic/NormalForm.lean) | Derive the required bounds and coefficient formulas for the S-idelic products. Local meromorphic order does not calculate overlap between Euler factors at different places. |
| 7.3–7.5, pp. 340–380. Levels, strong topologies, strong coprimality | GaussianField’s smooth circle model above covers a source of scalar basis estimates. Mathlib `WithSeminorms.tendsto_nhds` gives the criterion for convergence in specified seminorms. [seminorm topology](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/LocallyConvex/WithSeminorms.lean) | No equivalent of the paper’s absolute/invariant Paley–Wiener levels, p-primary orbital quotients, or strongly coprime idelic eigendistributions was verified. In §7.5, p. 374, Masullo expressly describes the strong-coprimality work there as unnecessary for the main trace calculation. |
| 9.1–9.2, pp. 395–419. Hardy–Sobolev and Paley–Wiener | Mathlib `mellin_eq_fourier` and `mellinInv_mellin_eq` identify a vertical line with a Fourier transform and give inversion under integral/continuity hypotheses. `SCV.paley_wiener_half_line_explicit` gives holomorphic extension to the upper half-plane and distributional boundary recovery from one-sided Fourier support. [Mellin inversion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/MellinInversion.lean) · [half-line Paley–Wiener](https://github.com/mrdouglasny/os-reconstruction/blob/a63f143281ef1810f6acbf90f6959cf579639f1b/OSReconstruction/SCV/PaleyWiener.lean) | Check the side on which the paper puts its weight: Definitions 9.1.2.1 and 9.2.1.1 use the logarithmic module and vertical-line norms. Establish the stated isometry, completions and support projections. Euclidean `TemperedDistribution.MemSobolev` alone does not identify these spaces. |
| 9.3, pp. 419–432. Approximate units | `TauCeti.L1GroupAlgebra.exists_isApproximateUnit_norm_eq_one` constructs two-sided, norm-one approximate units for the L¹ group algebra. [group algebra](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/8794ab329bb60340fa690a2902cf995f0571721b/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Algebra/GroupAlgebra/ApproximateIdentity.lean) | Show that the chosen kernels act and converge with the support and derivative controls required on the Hardy–Sobolev modules. |
| 10.1–10.2, pp. 434–447. Completion and spectral bases | Use the Mellin identities, smooth Fourier series and biorthogonal coordinate models above. | No reusable theorem establishing Masullo’s spectral Markushevich basis, totality of its dual, or identification of its elements with zeros was verified. A GitHub search for “Markushevich” also retrieves references to the complex-analysis author. |
| 10.3–10.4, pp. 447–474. Spectral nuclearity and trace | `PhyslibAlpha.ProbabilisticTheory.trace_mul_cycle` proves cyclicity for bounded and trace-class endomorphisms of a complete complex Hilbert space. `PhyslibAlpha.ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.summable_diagonal_of_hilbertSchmidt` controls an operator diagonal in a Hilbert basis. [trace algebra](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/b8f4133308bdc121c93b9d01f7be0ef1b0687d9b/PhyslibAlpha/ProbabilisticTheory/HilbertSpace/TraceClass/TraceAlgebra.lean) · [Hilbert–Schmidt](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/b8f4133308bdc121c93b9d01f7be0ef1b0687d9b/PhyslibAlpha/ProbabilisticTheory/HilbertSpace/TraceClass/HilbertSchmidt.lean) | Supply trace-class estimates for the particular spectral/geometric cutoffs and justify the passage to a nonorthogonal Markushevich basis. The operator facts do not furnish the equality with the zero sum. |
| C.1, pp. 657–670. Locally convex and inductive-limit topologies | Mathlib has `WithSeminorms`, `BarrelledSpace` and `MontelSpace`. The latter encodes compactness of closed von Neumann bounded sets. `TauCeti.FinalLocallyConvexTopology.continuous_iff_continuous_comp` provides the final locally convex topology’s mapping property. [seminorms](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/LocallyConvex/WithSeminorms.lean) · [barrelled spaces](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/LocallyConvex/Barrelled.lean) · [Montel convention](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/LocallyConvex/Montel.lean) · [final topology](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/8794ab329bb60340fa690a2902cf995f0571721b/TauCeti/Analysis/LocallyConvex/FinalTopology.lean) | Check sequential strictness, quasi-completeness and bounded lifting separately. Add the paper’s barrelledness assumption explicitly when using its meaning of “Montel.” |
| C.2, pp. 670–693. Tensor products, nuclearity and kernels | `PiTensorProduct.liftIsometry` is the finite-family projective-seminorm universal property on seminormed spaces. `GaussianField.schwartzTensorEquiv` is a continuous linear equivalence for the library’s nuclear tensor product of **real Euclidean** Schwartz spaces in positive dimensions. `ContinuousLinearMap.existsUnique_kernelOperator_eq` in TauCeti represents an operator from real test functions to complex distributions by a unique kernel on a product of Euclidean open sets. [Mathlib tensor](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/PiTensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean) · [Schwartz tensor](https://github.com/mrdouglasny/gaussian-field/blob/1283a2721377a36e80672799fcc1f69a494c8ea0/SchwartzNuclear/SchwartzTensorProduct.lean) · [kernel theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/8794ab329bb60340fa690a2902cf995f0571721b/TauCeti/Analysis/Distribution/SchwartzKernel.lean) | Use the two kernel results for their specific test spaces. C.2 and D.1.8 require the appropriate completed locally convex tensor topology, scalar field and identification with the adelic test space. |
| C.3, pp. 693–708. Nuclear and trace-class operators | Physlib has trace cyclicity (above) and `PhyslibAlpha.ProbabilisticTheory.trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis_of_nonneg`. TauCeti relates nuclear operators and summability of singular values in Hilbert spaces. [trace in a basis](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/b8f4133308bdc121c93b9d01f7be0ef1b0687d9b/PhyslibAlpha/ProbabilisticTheory/HilbertSpace/TraceClass/Basic.lean) · [nuclear comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/8794ab329bb60340fa690a2902cf995f0571721b/TauCeti/Analysis/OperatorIdeal/Nuclear/Comparison.lean) | For C.3.7.1 prove diagonal regularization for a measurable kernel on a Radon space. Basis diagonals and pointwise kernel diagonals are different objects. Masullo cites Brislawn, Thm. 3.1 p. 235 and Cor. 3.2 p. 237. |
| C.4, pp. 708–719. Pettis integration | `ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm` proves that scalar testing commutes with Bochner integration in complete normed spaces. [Bochner integral](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/ContinuousLinearMap.lean) | C.4.3.5 gives existence for compactly supported continuous functions with values in a quasi-complete Hausdorff locally convex space against a finite complex Radon measure. The Phillips counterexample and results on Pettis measurability or the Dunford–Pettis property do not prove this criterion. |
| C.5, pp. 719–742. Vector-valued holomorphy | Mathlib’s meromorphic normal form and order already allow normed vector targets. [normal form](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fc4f59e577feb1a4956671bc04ac18aaaf8cd842/Mathlib/Analysis/Meromorphic/NormalForm.lean) | The paper uses a quasi-complete locally convex target and weak integrals. Check whether each application lands in a Banach space before trying to reuse that API. |
| D.1, pp. 745–792. LCA Schwartz–Bruhat spaces | For Euclidean input, `GaussianField.schwartz_dyninMityaginSpace` gives a Hermite expansion for real Schwartz functions on a nontrivial finite-dimensional inner-product space. See the Euclidean kernel results above and the number-field and discrete-cocompact Poisson results in the main report. [Schwartz nuclearity](https://github.com/mrdouglasny/gaussian-field/blob/1283a2721377a36e80672799fcc1f69a494c8ea0/SchwartzNuclear/HermiteNuclear.lean) | The construction by structural pairs on an arbitrary locally compact abelian group, its LF topology and distributional Poisson theorem remain separate. |
| D.2–D.3, pp. 792–822. Modulus, isotypes, exponential decay | `MellinPaleyWiener.differentiable_and_forall_decay_and_inversion_of_contDiff_of_hasCompactSupport` proves entire extension, rapid decay uniformly on bounded vertical strips, and inversion for a compactly supported smooth scalar profile in log coordinates. Combine with Peter–Weyl on the compact factor and `mellin_eq_fourier` on the real factor. [Mellin–Paley–Wiener](https://github.com/anthropics/fermats-last-theorem/blob/6e837e75355538c7f80bab5b956861e86c4eacc2/Theorems/Thm_MellinPaleyWiener_differentiable_and_forall_decay_and_inversion_of_contDiff_of_hasCompactSupport.lean) | Compactly supported profiles give a starting test class. D.3.3.13 needs the topological isomorphism on the whole space with prescribed exponential decay, componentwise in the compact-factor characters. |

**Verification.** All links pin inspected source files. The projects linked here are Apache-2.0. Mathlib and Physlib use Lean 4.36.0, TauCeti uses 4.37.0-rc1, GaussianField uses 4.33.0-rc1, OSReconstruction uses 4.35.0-rc4 and Anthropic uses 4.33.1. The Mathlib names elaborated in `ScoutAnalysisChecks.lean`. The two local axiom checks for circle Fourier expansion's Hilbert basis and Mellin inversion returned only the three permitted axioms. External declarations were inspected with proof bodies and without direct proof holes. This source inspection alone leaves transitive axioms unverified.
